repositories.readme:
# Mailflare A self-hosted alternative to Google Workspace. Setup **custom domain Emails**, **Calendar, Drive, Booking** and **built-in AI agents**. Run it on Cloudflare or Docker. Send and receive with Cloudflare, Resend or Amazon SES. Store files in R2, Backblaze B2 or AWS S3. Use D1, Postgres, MySQL or Turso for the database. [![Deploy to Cloudflare](https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/button)](https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/?url=https://github.com/hieunc229/mailflare) ## Screenshots

Inbox
Domains
Mailboxes

Calendar
Booking
Drive
### Sponsors   Want to support Mailflare? [Become a sponsor](https://store.paymug.co/buy/mailflare-sponsor). ## Features ### Apps - **Email**: Custom domain mailboxes, personal or shared, with access you control. Send and receive with Cloudflare Email, Resend or Amazon SES. - **Routing rules**: Store, forward, reject or sort incoming mail. - **Calendar**: Repeating events with time zones. Attendees get email invitations. - **Booking**: Share a public link so anyone can book a free time on your calendar. - **Drive**: Store and share files. - **AI agents**: Search mail, draft replies and manage events. Connect other AI tools over MCP. ### Technical - **Databases**: Cloudflare D1 (default), PostgreSQL, MySQL, Turso / libSQL, or a local SQLite file. Set `DATABASE_URL` to switch. Works with Supabase, Neon, PlanetScale, TiDB and more. See [Databases](docs/databases.md). - **File storage**: Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2 or AWS S3. - **Hosting**: Cloudflare Workers or a single Docker container. - **Admin**: Users, API keys, webhooks, audit logs and backups. - **Import**: Bring in mail from IMAP, Gmail Takeout, `.eml` and `.mbox` files. Mailflare currently supports 34 languages, including English, Português (Brasil), Português (Portugal), Español, Français, Deutsch, Italiano, Nederlands, Polski, Українська, Русский, Türkçe, 中文（简体）, 日本語, 한국어, Bahasa Indonesia, Bahasa Melayu, Tiếng Việt, ไทย, हिन्दी, বাংলা, मराठी, తెలుగు, தமிழ், ગુજરાતી, ಕನ್ನಡ, മലയാളം, ਪੰਜਾਬੀ, සිංහල, Kiswahili, Hausa, plus العربية, اردو and فارسی (right-to-left). ## Cost You can receive and send mail for free. - **Receiving**: Cloudflare Email Routing is free. - **Sending**: Use the free tier of Resend (3,000 emails a month) or Amazon SES. Cloudflare's own sending needs the $5/month Paid Worker plan. New Amazon SES accounts start in a sandbox. Ask AWS for production access to lift it. Prices change, so check [Resend](https://resend.com/pricing), [Amazon SES](https://aws.amazon.com/ses/pricing/) and [Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/). ## Deploy 1. **Deploy the app.** Click **Deploy to Cloudflare**. Keep the app name `mailflare`, or it will break. 2. **Finish setup.** Open the app at `/setup` and create your admin account. 3. **Connect a domain.** Add a domain from the same Cloudflare account, then create your first mailbox. > **`CF_TOKEN` is required.** Create a scoped [Cloudflare API token](https://github.com/hieunc229/mailflare/issues/24#issuecomment-5523686105) with these permissions: > > - All accounts: Email Sending:Edit, DNS Settings:Edit, Email Routing Addresses:Edit > - All zones: DNS Settings:Edit, Email Routing Rules:Edit, Zone Settings:Edit, DNS:Edit More options: [deployment guide](docs/deployment.md). ### Deploy with an AI agent Paste this into an AI agent that has terminal access (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and similar): ```text Install Mailflare for me from https://github.com/hieunc229/mailflare on my Cloudflare account. 1. Read README.md, docs/deployment.md and wrangler.jsonc first. 2. Ask me for my Cloudflare account ID and two API tokens, using a secret input: a deploy token (for Wrangler) and a runtime token (the Worker secret CF_TOKEN). Never print them, commit them, or pass them as command arguments. 3. Keep the Worker name exactly "mailflare". Create or reuse the D1 database "mailflare", the R2 bucket "mailflare-raw", and the queues "mailflare-inbound", "mailflare-outbound" and "mailflare-agent". 4. Install dependencies, run `npm run deploy`, and set CF_TOKEN as a Worker secret. Do not run remote database migrations yourself. The /setup page does that. 5. Give me the app URL and anything I still need to do. I will open /setup, create the admin account and connect my domain. ``` Token permissions and more options: [deployment guide](docs/deployment.md#deploy-with-an-ai-coding-agent). ### Self-host with Docker Runs as one container on any server, with SQLite and local files. ```bash cp .env.docker.example .env.docker docker compose up -d --build ``` See [self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md). ## Local development ```bash cp .dev.vars.example .dev.vars npm install npm run db:migrate:local npm run dev ``` Add your Cloudflare credentials to `.dev.vars`, then open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Run `npm run db:seed` to load sample data. - `npm run build`: build the Worker - `npm run deploy`: build and deploy - `npm run lint`: lint and type check A schema change needs a migration for each database type. See [Databases](docs/databases.md#migrations). ## Documentation - [Deployment and configuration](docs/deployment.md) - [Databases](docs/databases.md) - [Sending and receiving providers](docs/providers.md) - [API and integrations](docs/api.md) - [Email assistant and MCP](docs/email-assistant-and-mcp.md) - [Adding a language](docs/localization.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) ## License See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

repositories.name: rakazo
repositories.description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative. Choose your own model and sandbox.
repositories.readme:
# Rakazo [English](./README.md) | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](./README.ja.md) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/elie222/rakazo?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&color=2563EB)](https://github.com/elie222/rakazo/stargazers) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join%20the%20community-5865F2?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/RWwKa2Sn7h) [![Download on the App Store](https://img.shields.io/badge/App%20Store-Download%20for%20iPhone-black?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://apps.apple.com/app/rakazo/id6801531099) [![Get Android on Google Play](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Play-Get%20the%20app-black?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&logo=googleplay&logoColor=white)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.rakazo.app) ![Rakazo — AI teammates you actually own](./docs/readme-hero.png) Rakazo is an open source, self-hosted alternative to Grok Bot. Persistent AI teammates with their own memory, routines, apps, and computer. Run it on your own machine, with your own model. Use it on the [web](https://app.rakazo.com), [desktop](https://rakazo.com/download/), [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/app/rakazo/id6801531099), and [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.rakazo.app). It is also an alternative to Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Instinct, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and Claude Duet. Learn more at [rakazo.com](https://rakazo.com). ## Features - Routines - Memory - Computer and browser use - Private or shared team computers - Sandboxes in Docker, the cloud, or on your own machine - Group chats - Delegation and subagents - Builds dashboards and docs you can share by link - Voice chat and calls - Any model, with your own keys - Thousands of app integrations, plus MCP
### Every bot gets a computer A browser, terminal, files, and a full desktop. Watch it work, take control to sign in, and hand it back. ### Bots that work together Put bots in a group and @mention them. They split the work, check each other, and report back.
### Routines Run a bot on a schedule, from an email, or from a webhook, and see every run. ### Pages Bots build live dashboards and documents you can open full screen, share, and ask about.
### Connected apps Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion, Linear and thousands more, plus your own MCP servers and OpenAPI tools. ### On every device Web, desktop, iPhone, iPad, and Android, all talking to the same server.
## Quick start (published images) You need Docker Engine, the Compose plugin, curl, and OpenSSL. No clone or Node install. ```bash mkdir -p rakazo && cd rakazo && curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elie222/rakazo/main/infra/compose/install-images.sh && bash install-images.sh ``` The installer downloads the Compose files, creates `.env` with random secrets, and starts Rakazo. It preserves an existing `.env` when rerun. Open [http://127.0.0.1:5173](http://127.0.0.1:5173), create an account, and connect a model. Local Docker computers are on by default. Optional remote providers: `e2b`, `novita`, `daytona`, `createos`, `boat`, `boxd`, `instabox`, or `railway` with the matching API key. New installs default to `latest` (stable releases, `linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`). A stable release must exist; setup does not fall back to main builds. Details and tags: [self-hosting guide](./docs/self-host.md#published-images-no-checkout). On restricted networks, override the installer download base (`RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_BASE`), skip existing Compose files (`--local` / `RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_SKIP_EXISTING`), or mirror the bootstrap script URL — see [Restricted networks / mirror downloads](./docs/self-host.md#restricted-networks--mirror-downloads). For an agent-assisted install, use [SETUP_PROMPT.md](./SETUP_PROMPT.md). ## Run on a server Bots stay on when the backend runs on a server. Use the same installer on a VPS, then connect from the desktop app, the mobile app, or a browser. ```bash bash install-images.sh --prepare-only # edit .env: SANDBOX_PROVIDER=boat (or e2b / daytona / createos) with its API key, RAKAZO_HOST=your.domain bash install-images.sh ``` Put HTTPS in front of port 5173; [docs/self-host-production.md](./docs/self-host-production.md#public-single-vm-deployment) covers the Caddy setup and host hardening. In the desktop app choose **Existing instance** and enter the `https://` address. Or [deploy on Railway](https://railway.com/new/template/rakazo-template); see the [Railway setup guide](./infra/railway/README.md). ## Local development (source checkout) You need Node.js 24.15.0 or newer in the 24.x line, or Node.js 26+; pnpm 12; and Docker. Node.js 25.x is not supported. ```bash git clone https://github.com/elie222/rakazo.git cd rakazo cp .env.example .env ``` Set `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `POSTGRES_APP_PASSWORD` to two values from `openssl rand -hex 16`, then put them in `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` and `DATABASE_URL`. The app connects as its own `rakazo_app` login, which row-level security applies to; migrations run as the owner ([database roles](docs/self-host-configuration.md#database-roles)). Set `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, and `SCREEN_PROXY_SECRET` to independent long random values. Docker sandboxes also need a dedicated `SANDBOX_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN`. You can also set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, or connect a supported model provider during onboarding. For host-side development with Docker Desktop, set `SANDBOX_CONTROL_VIA_LOOPBACK=true` in `.env`. The supervisor discovers Docker Desktop's user socket automatically; `DOCKER_HOST` or `DOCKER_SOCKET` can override it for another Docker runtime. Managed app catalogs are optional. Set `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` for Composio, or the `PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_ID`, `PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `PIPEDREAM_PROJECT_ID` trio for Pipedream Connect. Users can add an HTTPS MCP server or OpenAPI JSON document from **Integrations** without enabling either managed catalog. Local (stdio) MCP servers are off until you set `MCP_STDIO_ENABLED=true` and list their commands in `MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_COMMANDS`; see [Tools and integrations](./docs/self-host-integrations.md). Connector credentials are encrypted on the server and are never returned by the API. Paid data services (map places, search results, work emails, profiles, SEO data) are optional too. Set `PAID_SERVICES_PROVIDER=treg` and `PAID_SERVICES_API_KEY` to an org-scoped [Treg](https://treg.to) token, and bots can find and call them on the deployment's account. When model credits are on, each call is charged to the organization's credits at the provider's cost plus 20%. ```bash pnpm install pnpm sandbox:build pnpm dev ``` `pnpm dev` uses the Postgres in `DATABASE_URL` when it accepts a connection. Otherwise it starts a local `rakazo-dev-postgres` container with Docker, and every checkout reuses that one. It applies migrations and generates the Prisma client before starting. A branch that adds migrations main doesn't have gets its own database on the same server, copied from the shared one when possible, so unmerged schema changes stay out of it. When the default ports are taken, for example by another git worktree, it moves to the next free block and prints the URL. Set `WEB_PORT` and `API_PORT` to choose ports yourself. To try a checkout from your phone or another computer, install [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com) on each device and set `RAKAZO_DEV_TAILNET=1` in `.env`. `pnpm dev` then serves the web app over HTTPS at `https://..ts.net:`, reachable only from devices on your tailnet, and stops serving it when you quit. Sign in at that URL on every device, including the one running it. The first run may ask you to turn on HTTPS certificates for your tailnet. To keep keys in a secrets manager instead of `.env`, set `RAKAZO_DEV_RUN_WITH` to the command that runs another with your secrets added, for example `op run --env-file=dev.env --` or `infisical run --env=dev --projectId= --`. `pnpm dev` then starts inside it, and the values it adds win over `.env`. To run Postgres from the Compose file instead, start it with the `postgres-host` overlay, which publishes loopback `127.0.0.1:5433`, and point `DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` at it: ```bash docker compose --env-file .env \ -f infra/compose/docker-compose.yml \ -f infra/compose/docker-compose.postgres-host.yml \ up postgres -d ``` Use a URI-safe `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` (`openssl rand -hex 16`). An existing `pgdata` volume keeps the user, password, and database from first init, so keep those values in `.env`, or change them in place with `ALTER ROLE` / rename. Recreate the volume only after a backup (or when the data is disposable); `docker compose down -v` deletes all Postgres state. Open the printed URL ([http://127.0.0.1:5173](http://127.0.0.1:5173) by default), create an account, connect a model, and create your first bot. For deployment, provider selection, backups, and upgrades, see the [self-hosting guide](./docs/self-host.md), [production deployment](./docs/self-host-production.md), [backup and restore](./docs/self-host-backups.md), and [upgrading](./docs/self-host-upgrading.md). To use CreateOS, set `SANDBOX_PROVIDER=createos` and `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_API_KEY`. Optional `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_BASE_URL`, `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_SHAPE`, and `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_ROOTFS` default to `https://api.sb.createos.sh`, `s-2vcpu-2gb`, and `desktop:1`. To use Railway computers, set `SANDBOX_PROVIDER=railway`, `RAILWAY_API_TOKEN` and `RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_ID` on the API and worker. Choose the sandbox environment explicitly; Railway's automatic environment ID identifies the hosted app's environment. Use the narrowest Railway API token that works: prefer a project token if sufficient for sandbox operations and supported by the client's authentication. This provider currently uses bearer authentication, so use a team/workspace token rather than a personal account token. The live screen and desktop require `PRIVATE` networking so Railway's public domain can serve the screen. Computers use this mode and can reach other services in the same Railway project/environment, as well as the public internet. We recommend a dedicated Railway project (or at least a separate environment) for sandboxes, separate from the app and database. Recreate existing `ISOLATED` computers before use. The desktop is installed on first start. Stopping a computer saves its portable home and destroys the sandbox; the next start restores that home in a new sandbox. Railway sandbox usage is metered. New computers start in Railway's default region. Set `RAILWAY_SANDBOX_REGION` (for example `asia-southeast1-eqsg3a`) to keep them near the API; a running computer moves on its next start. Workspace exports reject files above 64 MiB without truncating them. Set `RAILWAY_MAX_WORKSPACE_FILE_BYTES` to change this limit. ## Desktop and mobile The Electron and Expo apps are clients of the same Rakazo API used by the web app. With the development stack running, launch Electron with: ```bash pnpm --filter @rakazo/desktop dev ``` On first run the desktop app asks whether to run Rakazo on this computer or connect to an existing server. **This computer** can run without Docker on Apple silicon Macs with macOS 26 or later when the build includes a server bundle. Fresh setups use this path: the app downloads the server and computer runtime as needed. Existing Docker setups are offered a move while Docker is running; choosing **Keep Docker** leaves them on Docker. Other builds and platforms use Docker Compose to install and start the published images (the same files as `infra/compose/install-images.sh`) under the app's data directory. This path needs Docker Desktop, OrbStack, or Docker Engine. Without one, setup offers the Docker Desktop download, opens an installed Docker app that is not running, and continues on its own once Docker answers. Installed builds pin the image tag to their own version; unpackaged builds pull `edge`. Developers running `pnpm dev` should pick **Existing instance** with `http://127.0.0.1:5173` instead. Public servers must use HTTPS; HTTP is accepted only for loopback and private LAN addresses (not link-local). The app verifies Rakazo's health endpoint before saving, and later launches go straight to that instance. The Docker stack keeps running after the app quits; the Docker-free server stops with the app. **Quit and Stop Bots** in the application menu stops the managed stack and quits; switching to another server also stops it. On Linux the desktop app ships as an AppImage, which needs FUSE 2 (`libfuse.so.2`). Distributions that only include FUSE 3, such as Fedora Silverblue or Ubuntu 24.04, show `dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2`. Install the FUSE 2 library (`fuse-libs` on Fedora, `libfuse2t64` on Ubuntu 24.04, `libfuse2` on older Ubuntu and Debian), or run the AppImage without FUSE: ```bash chmod +x Rakazo-*.AppImage ./Rakazo-*.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run ``` The Docker path of **This computer** looks for the `docker` CLI and does not detect Podman. To try another Docker-compatible CLI that supports the `compose` commands, set `RAKAZO_DOCKER_BINARY` to its path before starting the app. Use **Change Rakazo Server…** in the application menu to reconnect. Closing that window without saving returns to the previous instance. For development automation, set `RAKAZO_WEB_URL` to point the shell somewhere else without changing the saved instance, or `RAKAZO_FORCE_SETUP=1` to run setup again. Mobile build and release instructions live in [docs/mobile-release.md](./docs/mobile-release.md). ## UI language The web (and Electron-hosted) UI supports English, Deutsch, 한국어, Türkçe, हिन्दी, Português (Brasil), 简体中文, 繁體中文, Español, Русский, Français, עברית, Nederlands, 日本語, and Polski under **Settings → Language**. The Expo app ships the same 15 languages under **Account → Language**. A device language or `EXPO_PUBLIC_DEFAULT_UI_LOCALE` still selects the starting catalog before a saved choice. Native Electron setup and menus also support the web UI's languages, following the saved app choice or, on first launch, the system language. The marketing homepage (`apps/www`) offers all 15 languages through footer links, including `/zh/` and `/zh-tw/`; other marketing pages remain primarily English. ## Development ```text apps/ web, api, worker, desktop, mobile, and public website packages/ domain, contracts, persistence, adapters, UI, and test tooling infra/ local services and computer images docs/ architecture, operations, and release guides ``` Common checks: ```bash pnpm lint pnpm check pnpm test pnpm test:integration pnpm test:e2e ``` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for the development workflow and test matrix. ## Documentation Chinese guides cover [self-hosting](./docs/zh-CN/self-host.md), [models](./docs/zh-CN/self-host-models.md), [backups](./docs/zh-CN/self-host-backups.md), [upgrading](./docs/zh-CN/self-host-upgrading.md), and [restricted networks](./docs/zh-CN/self-host-restricted-network.md). - [Self-hosting](./docs/self-host.md) - [Self-host configuration](./docs/self-host-configuration.md) - [Self-host secrets](./docs/self-host-secrets.md) - [Sign-in and accounts](./docs/self-host-accounts.md) - [Models](./docs/self-host-models.md) - [Tools and integrations](./docs/self-host-integrations.md) - [Computer providers](./docs/self-host-sandbox-providers.md) - [Docker computers](./docs/self-host-docker-computers.md) - [Kubernetes / k3s installation](./docs/self-host-kubernetes.md) ([한국어](./docs/ko-KR/self-host-kubernetes.md)) - [Storage and encryption](./docs/self-host-storage.md) - [Production deployment](./docs/self-host-production.md) - [Backup and restore](./docs/self-host-backups.md) - [Upgrading](./docs/self-host-upgrading.md) - [Logs and monitoring](./docs/self-host-observability.md) - [Audit log](./docs/self-host-audit-log.md) - [Apps and clients](./docs/self-host-clients.md) - [Billing](./docs/self-host-billing.md) - [Computer runtime and isolation](./docs/computer-runtime.md) - [Desktop releases](./docs/desktop-release.md) - [Mobile releases](./docs/mobile-release.md) - [Performance testing](./docs/performance.md) - [Bots that manage bots](./docs/fleet-management.md) ## How Rakazo compares - [Grok Bot](https://rakazo.com/grok-bot-alternative/) - [Muse](https://rakazo.com/muse-alternative/) - [Dots](https://rakazo.com/dots-alternative/) - [Instinct](https://rakazo.com/instinct-alternative/) - [OpenClaw](https://rakazo.com/openclaw-alternative/) - [Hermes Agent](https://rakazo.com/hermes-alternative/) - [All comparisons](https://rakazo.com/alternatives/) ## Thanks - [Inbox Zero](https://getinboxzero.com/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) - [PromptLayer](https://promptlayer.com/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) - [ConnectorMap](https://connectormap.luinbytes.dev/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) - [CodeRabbit](https://www.coderabbit.ai/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) - [Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) - [Snyk](https://snyk.io/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) - [Incredibuild](https://www.incredibuild.com/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) ## Stack - TypeScript - React 19, Vite, and Tailwind CSS - Electron and Expo - Hono and oRPC - PostgreSQL and Prisma - Better Auth - Graphile Worker - Pi - Docker, E2B, Daytona, CreateOS, and Boat - Composio, Pipedream Connect, MCP, and OpenAPI integrations ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request. For security vulnerabilities, follow [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of filing a public issue. Rakazo is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](./LICENSE). Questions and ideas are welcome in the [Rakazo Discord community](https://discord.gg/RWwKa2Sn7h).

repositories.name: spring-boot
repositories.description: Spring Boot helps you to create Spring-powered, production-grade applications and services with absolute minimum fuss.
repositories.readme:
= Spring Boot image:https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/actions/workflows/build-and-deploy-snapshot.yml/badge.svg?branch=main["Build Status", link="https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/actions/workflows/build-and-deploy-snapshot.yml?query=branch%3Amain"] image:https://img.shields.io/badge/Revved%20up%20by-Develocity-06A0CE?logo=Gradle&labelColor=02303A["Revved up by Develocity", link="https://ge.spring.io/scans?&search.rootProjectNames=Spring%20Boot%20Build&search.rootProjectNames=spring-boot-build"]

:docs: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot
:github: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot

Spring Boot helps you to create Spring-powered, production-grade applications and services with absolute minimum fuss.
It takes an opinionated view of the Spring platform so that new and existing users can quickly get to the bits they need.

You can use Spring Boot to create stand-alone Java applications that can be started using `java -jar` or more traditional WAR deployments.
We also provide a command-line tool that runs Spring scripts.

Our primary goals are:

* Provide a radically faster and widely accessible getting started experience for all Spring development.
* Be opinionated, but get out of the way quickly as requirements start to diverge from the defaults.
* Provide a range of non-functional features common to large classes of projects (for example, embedded servers, security, metrics, health checks, externalized configuration).
* Absolutely no code generation and no requirement for XML configuration.



== Installation and Getting Started

The {docs}[reference documentation] includes detailed {docs}/installing.html[installation instructions] as well as a comprehensive {docs}/tutorial/first-application/index.html[``getting started``] guide.

Here is a quick teaser of a complete Spring Boot application in Java:

[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.boot.*;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.*;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.*;

@RestController
@SpringBootApplication
public class Example {

	@RequestMapping("/")
	String home() {
		return "Hello World!";
	}

	public static void main(String[] args) {
		SpringApplication.run(Example.class, args);
	}

}
----



== Getting Help

Are you having trouble with Spring Boot? We want to help!

* Check the {docs}/[reference documentation], especially the {docs}/how-to/index.html[How-to's] -- they provide solutions to the most common questions.
* Learn the Spring basics -- Spring Boot builds on many other Spring projects; check the https://spring.io[spring.io] website for a wealth of reference documentation.
  If you are new to Spring, try one of the https://spring.io/guides[guides].
* If you are upgrading, read the {github}/wiki[release notes] for upgrade instructions and "new and noteworthy" features.
* Ask a question -- we monitor https://stackoverflow.com[stackoverflow.com] for questions tagged with https://stackoverflow.com/tags/spring-boot[`spring-boot`].
* Report bugs with Spring Boot at {github}/issues[github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues].



== Contributing

We welcome contributions of all kinds!
Please read our link:CONTRIBUTING.adoc[contribution guidelines] before submitting a pull request.



== Reporting Issues

Spring Boot uses GitHub's integrated issue tracking system to record bugs and feature requests.
If you want to raise an issue, please follow the recommendations below:

* Before you log a bug, please search the {github}/issues[issue tracker] to see if someone has already reported the problem.
* If the issue doesn't already exist, {github}/issues/new[create a new issue].
* Please provide as much information as possible with the issue report.
We like to know the Spring Boot version, operating system, and JVM version you're using.
* If you need to paste code or include a stack trace, use Markdown.
+++```+++ escapes before and after your text.
* If possible, try to create a test case or project that replicates the problem and attach it to the issue.



== Building from Source

You don't need to build from source to use Spring Boot.
If you want to try out the latest and greatest, Spring Boot can be built and published to your local Maven cache using the https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/gradle_wrapper.html[Gradle wrapper].
You also need JDK 25.

[source,shell]
----
$ ./gradlew publishToMavenLocal
----

This command builds all modules and publishes them to your local Maven cache.
It won't run any of the tests.
If you want to build everything, use the `build` task:

[source,shell]
----
$ ./gradlew build
----



== Guides

The https://spring.io/[spring.io] site contains several guides that show how to use Spring Boot step-by-step:

* https://spring.io/guides/gs/spring-boot/[Building an Application with Spring Boot] is an introductory guide that shows you how to create an application, run it, and add some management services.
* https://spring.io/guides/gs/actuator-service/[Building a RESTful Web Service with Spring Boot Actuator] is a guide to creating a REST web service and also shows how the server can be configured.



== License

Spring Boot is Open Source software released under the https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.html[Apache 2.0 license].

# lodash v4.18.1 [Site](https://lodash.com/) | [Docs](https://lodash.com/docs) | [FP Guide](https://github.com/lodash/lodash/wiki/FP-Guide) | [Contributing](https://github.com/lodash/lodash/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) | [Wiki](https://github.com/lodash/lodash/wiki "Changelog, Roadmap, etc.") | [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/openjs-foundation/cross-project-council/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) | [Governance](https://github.com/lodash/lodash/blob/HEAD/GOVERNANCE.md) | [Twitter](https://twitter.com/bestiejs) | [Chat](https://gitter.im/lodash/lodash) > [!IMPORTANT] > As announced on the [OpenJS Foundation blog](https://openjsf.org/blog/sta-supports-lodash), Lodash has received support from the Sovereign Tech Agency and will transition to the Feature-Complete maturity stage so that it remains stable, secure, and sustainable long-term. As part of this effort, Lodash is rebooting its governance. A draft charter will be published shortly. The upcoming Technical Steering Committee (TSC) is already at work. For transparency, its members are listed in [GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/lodash/lodash/blob/HEAD/GOVERNANCE.md). The [Lodash](https://lodash.com/) library exported as a [UMD](https://github.com/umdjs/umd) module. Generated using [lodash-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lodash-cli): ```shell $ npm run build $ lodash -o ./dist/lodash.js $ lodash core -o ./dist/lodash.core.js ``` ## Download * [Core build](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lodash/lodash/4.18.1/dist/lodash.core.js) ([~4 kB gzipped](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lodash/lodash/4.18.1/dist/lodash.core.min.js)) * [Full build](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lodash/lodash/4.18.1/dist/lodash.js) ([~24 kB gzipped](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lodash/lodash/4.18.1/dist/lodash.min.js)) * [CDN copies](https://www.jsdelivr.com/projects/lodash) Lodash is released under the [MIT license](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lodash/lodash/4.18.1/LICENSE) & supports modern environments.
Review the [build differences](https://github.com/lodash/lodash/wiki/build-differences) & pick one that’s right for you. ## Installation In a browser: ```html ``` Using npm: ```shell $ npm i -g npm $ npm i --save lodash ``` In Node.js: ```js // Load the full build. var _ = require('lodash'); // Load the core build. var _ = require('lodash/core'); // Load the FP build for immutable auto-curried iteratee-first data-last methods. var fp = require('lodash/fp'); // Load method categories. var array = require('lodash/array'); var object = require('lodash/fp/object'); // Cherry-pick methods for smaller browserify/rollup/webpack bundles. var at = require('lodash/at'); var curryN = require('lodash/fp/curryN'); ``` ## Why Lodash? Lodash makes JavaScript easier by taking the hassle out of working with arrays,
numbers, objects, strings, etc. Lodash’s modular methods are great for: * Iterating arrays, objects, & strings * Manipulating & testing values * Creating composite functions ## Module Formats Lodash is available in a [variety of builds](https://lodash.com/custom-builds) & module formats. * [lodash](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lodash) & [per method packages](https://www.npmjs.com/browse/keyword/lodash-modularized) * [lodash-es](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lodash-es), [babel-plugin-lodash](https://www.npmjs.com/package/babel-plugin-lodash), & [lodash-webpack-plugin](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lodash-webpack-plugin) * [lodash/fp](https://github.com/lodash/lodash/tree/npm/fp) * [lodash-amd](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lodash-amd)

repositories.readme: # Hex Hex is local voice dictation for Mac, Windows and Linux. Hold a key, speak, and it pastes. ## How it works - hold the shortcut, speak, then let go - Hex transcribes on your device and pastes into whatever app you're in - the first run downloads a speech model; after that nothing leaves your machine - experimental features live in Labs, at the bottom of the sidebar ## What it does - hold the shortcut to dictate, or set Shortcut mode to Tap to start and stop with a press - the text lands at the cursor in whatever app you're in - Option-Shift-V pastes the last dictation again (Ctrl-Alt-V on Windows and Linux) - History keeps your dictations, searchable, for 7 days by default - Output runs every dictation through steps you choose (word replacements, built-in cleanups, your own scripts, an optional OpenCode rewrite), with different steps per app or website - Vocabulary is one list of names Hex should know; Whisper and Qwen3-ASR read it while transcribing, Parakeet models read it with Labs › Vocabulary help on, and the OpenCode rewrite uses it - Annotate records the screen while you draw and talk, on macOS, Linux and Windows (GNOME Wayland needs Labs › Annotate on GNOME) - an authenticated local API and the [TypeScript SDK](sdk/typescript/README.md) transcribe with the same model, for your own tools - Meetings is a macOS lab that records a call and writes the transcript Output and History: ## Speech models Hex downloads one model the first time it runs and transcribes with it on your machine from then on. On an English system that's Parakeet Unified English: it writes while you talk, so the text is ready when you let go. Other languages start with the model recommended for them. That model also serves meetings and `hex transcribe`. Settings' picker offers more, among others: - Parakeet v3: 25 European languages, and it hears which one you speak - Cohere Transcribe: the fewest wrong words, in 14 languages; a big download - Whisper large-v3-turbo: almost any language, and it reads your vocabulary - Qwen3-ASR 0.6B: Chinese and 29 more, and it reads your vocabulary - SenseVoice Small: Chinese, Japanese, Korean and English; a small download - Nemotron 3.5 ASR: writes while you talk, in 27 languages - Granite Speech 5.0: IBM's model, seven languages, with punctuation - one-language models: ivrit.ai Whisper for Hebrew, GigaAM v3 for Russian, NB-Whisper for Norwegian, QwenCleo-ASR for Egyptian Arabic - more English models: Parakeet v2 and Underdog Bark 3.0 Add a GGUF model of your own with "Add model file…" in the picker; see [your own speech models](docs/features/own-models.md). ## Downloads Stable is the current release. Dev is the newest build of `dev` and updates itself from the dev channel. | Platform | Stable | Dev | | --- | --- | --- | | macOS (Apple silicon) | [DMG](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/macos-arm64-dmg) | [DMG](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/macos-arm64-dmg) | | Windows x64 | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/windows-x64-setup) | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/windows-x64-setup) | | Windows ARM64 | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/windows-arm64-setup) | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/windows-arm64-setup) | | Linux x86_64 | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64) | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64) | | Linux x86_64 (Debian, Ubuntu) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64-deb) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64-deb) | | Linux x86_64 (Fedora, openSUSE) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64-rpm) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64-rpm) | | Linux ARM64 | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-arm64) | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-arm64) | | Linux ARM64 (Debian, Ubuntu) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-arm64-deb) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-arm64-deb) | | Linux ARM64 (Fedora, openSUSE) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-arm64-rpm) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-arm64-rpm) | Or install with: - Homebrew: `brew install --cask anomalyco/tap/hex` - AUR: `yay -S hex-bin` - install script (Linux): `curl -fsSL https://anoma.ly/hex/install-linux.sh | sh` - Nix (Linux): `nix profile add github:anomalyco/hex` ## Command line `hex transcribe meeting.m4a` prints a recording's transcript, whether or not the app is running. It reads WAV, AIFF, CAF, FLAC, MP3, Ogg, WebM, and MP4/M4A/MOV, including a video's soundtrack. The same `hex` controls the running app (`hex status`, `hex dictation`, `hex settings`); see [`docs/cli.md`](docs/cli.md). On macOS the CLI is inside the app. Homebrew links it for you; otherwise link it somewhere on your `PATH` that you own: ```sh ln -s /Applications/Hex.app/Contents/MacOS/hex ~/.local/bin/hex ``` Linux and Windows installs put `hex` on your `PATH`. More docs are in [`docs/`](docs/README.md). ## Contributing We don't take pull requests. [Open an issue](https://github.com/anomalyco/hex/issues) describing the bug or idea, and our agents usually turn it around fast. MIT licensed.

## ❤️ Sponsors

## Why DBX?

🪶 25 MB, zero runtime bloat

No Java JRE. No Python venv. No bundled Chromium. DBX ships as a single small binary — download, install, connect. DBeaver needs Java; TablePlus is Freemium. DBX runs everywhere with nothing extra.

🤖 AI that lives in your editor

Highlight a table, describe what you want, get SQL back — no copy-paste between tools. Works with Claude, OpenAI, or local models via Ollama. Built-in safety checks review AI-generated SQL before it runs.

🔌 MCP: your databases, AI-ready

DBX speaks the Model Context Protocol. Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and other AI coding agents can query your databases through connections you already set up. One config, everywhere.

🌐 Desktop + Docker + Web

Native app on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Self-host via Docker for team access. Web version for browser-only environments. Same feature set. Same connections.

📨 Not just databases

Message queues and middleware get first-class consoles: Kafka, RocketMQ, RabbitMQ, Pulsar, and MQTT, plus Nacos, Consul, ZooKeeper, and etcd. Inspect topics and messages next to your databases — no extra tool.

🧩 Plugin ecosystem

Extend DBX with signed, sandboxed plugins from the built-in store — S3, Kubernetes, LDAP, and more. Build your own with the Go / TypeScript SDK.
## Features ### 100+ Databases, One Tool MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Cloudflare D1, Redis, MongoDB, DuckDB, ClickHouse, SQL Server, Oracle, Elasticsearch, Easysearch, Meilisearch, CouchDB, Qdrant, Milvus, Weaviate, MariaDB, TiDB, OceanBase, openGauss, GaussDB, KWDB, KingbaseES, Vastbase, GoldenDB, Doris, SelectDB, StarRocks, Manticore Search, Redshift, DM, TDengine, XuguDB, CockroachDB, Access, HighGo, UXDB, Dolt, and more. Agent-based profiles extend DBX to H2, Snowflake, Trino, PrestoSQL, Hive, DB2, Informix, Neo4j, Cassandra, BigQuery, Cloud Spanner, Kylin, SunDB, JDBCX, and custom JDBC connections. New native and agent-driven drivers also cover Databricks, SAP HANA, Teradata, Vertica, Firebird, Exasol, YashanDB, GBase 8a/8s, Databend, RQLite, Turso, InfluxDB, QuestDB, IoTDB, etcd, ZooKeeper, Nacos, Consul KV, IRIS, and more. All in a single ~25 MB app. No bundled Chromium. ### Query Editor CodeMirror 6 with SQL syntax highlighting, metadata-aware autocomplete, `Cmd+Enter` execution, selected SQL execution, SQL formatting, diagnostics, and 9 editor themes. Persistent query history, saved SQL snippets, tab restore, and SQL file execution keep repeat work close at hand. ### AI SQL Assistant Describe what you want in plain language — get SQL back. DBX can explain queries, optimize SQL, fix errors, and run AI-generated SQL through built-in safety checks. Works with Claude, OpenAI, local models, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. ### Data Grid Virtual-scrolled table that handles large result sets. Inline editing, SQL preview before save, WHERE / ORDER BY controls, DataGrip-style filters, LIKE / NOT LIKE context filters, sorting, full-text search, pagination, column resize, auto-fit, row numbers, zebra stripes, and full cell details. Export or copy as CSV, JSON, Markdown, XLSX, or INSERT statements. ### Schema Tools - **Schema browser** — databases, schemas, tables, columns, indexes, foreign keys, triggers, with sidebar search & pin - **Object browser** — grouped procedures, functions, views, and source editing where supported - **Table structure editor** — reviewable column and index changes for supported engines - **ER diagram** — visualize table relationships - **Schema diff** — compare structures across connections - **Explain plan** — visual query execution plan - **Field lineage** — column-level lineage analysis - **Database search** — find objects across large schemas ### Data Operations - **Table import** — CSV, Excel - **Data transfer** — migrate between databases - **Database export** — full database dump - **Data compare** — compare table data and review synchronization output - **SQL file execution** — run `.sql` files directly - **File preview** — drag & drop Parquet, CSV, JSON to preview instantly (powered by DuckDB) - **Connection import** — bring connection profiles from DBeaver or Navicat ### Specialized Browsers - **Redis** — key pattern search, batch key operations, command runner, TTL editing, and all data types (String, Hash, List, Set, ZSet, Stream) - **MongoDB** — document CRUD with pagination, Atlas & replica set URL connection ### Message Queue & Middleware Consoles - **Kafka / RocketMQ / RabbitMQ / Pulsar** — topics, consumer groups, message browsing, query and trace, broker monitoring, permissions and policies - **MQTT** — topic tree navigation, subscribe, and publish - **Nacos / Consul / ZooKeeper / etcd** — service discovery, KV / config browsing, health, and ACL ### Plugin System - **Extensible by design** — new connection types and tools arrive as plugins: S3 browsing, Kubernetes, LDAP, and more from the built-in store - **Signed & sandboxed** — every plugin package is signature-verified before install; plugin UI runs sandboxed with its own sidecar process - **Build your own** — Go / TypeScript SDKs with `npx @dbx-app/plugin-cli` scaffolding; publish to the Marketplace via [`t8y2/dbx-store`](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx-store) ### Safety & Connectivity SSH tunnel (key & password) · database and AI proxy settings · auto-reconnect on connection loss · confirmation dialogs for destructive operations · encrypted config export/import · color-coded connections · driver store and optional JDBC plugin ### Polished UI Dark mode with native title bar sync · 9 editor themes · English, 简体中文 & Español · layout preferences · built-in auto-update ## AI Agent Integration (MCP) DBX provides a separate [Rust-powered MCP server](packages/mcp-server/) that lets AI coding agents query databases using connections configured in DBX. The MCP server is distributed independently from the desktop application, so installing DBX does not automatically install the MCP executable. ```bash npx @dbx-app/mcp-server ``` Add to your `.mcp.json`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "dbx": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@dbx-app/mcp-server"] } } } ``` Manage the connection allowlist and the **Read only**, **Data read/write**, and **Full access** modes in **DBX Settings → MCP**. The machine-readable values remain `read_only`, `safe_write`, and `high_risk_write`; client configs do not need permission or connection-scope environment variables. For upgrade compatibility, an existing `DBX_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=0` (or `false`) remains a read-only restriction only until a central MCP policy is saved for the first time; it can never enable writes or override a saved policy. Windows portable builds need `DBX_DATA_DIR` in the MCP config, pointing to the `data` directory next to `DBX.exe` (the folder that contains `dbx.db`). For DBX Web or Docker deployments, point the MCP server at the Web backend API. If the Web login page requires a password, set `DBX_WEB_PASSWORD` to the same password used there: ```json { "mcpServers": { "dbx": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@dbx-app/mcp-server"], "env": { "DBX_WEB_URL": "http://localhost:4224", "DBX_WEB_PASSWORD": "your-web-login-password" } } } } ``` Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and any MCP-compatible agent. Supports listing connections, browsing tables, executing SQL, and opening tables directly in DBX's UI. Precompiled native binaries are also published for macOS, Linux, and Windows in [package releases](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/releases?q=packages-v). They run without Node.js and are suitable for offline or server environments. The npm installation uses the same Rust binary through a small Node.js launcher. DBX also provides a dedicated CLI package for terminal, script, and Codex workflows: ```bash npm install -g @dbx-app/cli # or via Homebrew brew tap t8y2/tap && brew install dbx-cli dbx agent setup dbx connections list --json dbx query local "select 1" --json ``` The CLI includes the official DBX Agent Skill. `dbx agent setup` installs or updates it offline under `~/.agents/skills/dbx`, so shell-capable AI agents know how to use DBX CLI safely. See the [MCP server README](packages/mcp-server/README.md) and [CLI README](packages/cli/README.md) for details. ## Install Download the latest release from the [Releases](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/releases/latest) page. **Homebrew (macOS):** ```bash brew install --cask dbx ``` **Scoop (Windows):** ```bash scoop bucket add dbx https://github.com/t8y2/scoop-bucket scoop install dbx ``` **WinGet (Windows):** ``` winget install t8y2.dbx ``` **Flatpak (Linux):** ```bash flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flatpark https://dl.flatpark.org/flatpark.flatpakrepo flatpak install flatpark com.dbxio.dbx ``` Updates then arrive through the regular `flatpak update`. See the [DBX page on FlatPark](https://flatpark.org/apps/com.dbxio.dbx/) for details. ## Self-Hosted (Docker) For scheduled backups after closing the desktop app or browser, see [Background Database Backups](docs/background-database-backups.md), including Windows/macOS/Linux startup and persistent container backup volumes. DBX provides a web version that can be deployed via Docker. The examples use the `latest` tag to pull the current release. ```bash # The default keeps the key in the persistent /app/data volume. docker run -d --pull=always --name dbx -p 4224:4224 \ -v dbx-data:/app/data \ t8y2/dbx:latest ``` This uses the cross-platform `dbx-data` named volume. Users in China can use the CNB image, `docker.cnb.cool/dbxio.com/dbx:latest`, for faster pulls. For Docker Compose, `deploy/docker-compose.yml` remains the source-build configuration. To deploy a published image, use `deploy/docker-compose.release.yml`: ```bash docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.release.yml up -d ``` ```yaml services: dbx: image: t8y2/dbx:latest # For faster pulls in China, use the CNB image instead: # image: docker.cnb.cool/dbxio.com/dbx:latest pull_policy: always ports: - "4224:4224" volumes: - dbx-data:/app/data restart: unless-stopped volumes: dbx-data: ``` Open `http://localhost:4224` in your browser. Multi-arch images (amd64 / arm64) are available. Connection, plugin, AI, and tunnel credentials are encrypted before they are written to `dbx.db`. Desktop builds use the local platform credential store (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or Linux Secret Service). Web/Docker and directly running `dbx-web` use the same managed data-directory key by default: `${DBX_DATA_DIR}/.dbx/secret.key`. The key is created only when migration starts or the first sensitive value is written, and must be backed up together with `dbx.db`. Persisting `/app/data` is therefore sufficient for a normal Docker deployment. This key protects the database contents, but cannot protect the whole data volume if the volume itself is copied or exposed. Windows portable builds are the exception to the desktop platform-key rule. To remain portable across computers, they keep the local storage key at `data/.dbx/secret.key`; move and back up the complete `data` directory. If an older portable profile already contains ciphertext protected by Windows Credential Manager, launch the new build once on the original computer so DBX can verify and copy that key to the USB drive. If the original computer or key is gone, the ciphertext cannot be recovered automatically; restore the original key or a pre-migration backup. Keeping the key beside the database means anyone who obtains or copies the whole drive can also decrypt its credentials. For production deployments, replace the managed key with a Docker/Kubernetes Secret by setting `DBX_SECRET_KEY_FILE`, or provide `DBX_SECRET_KEY` through a secret manager. Explicit keys take precedence and must never be rotated while encrypted data is in use. Without a usable key, business APIs remain blocked and the browser displays the data security upgrade screen. When running the binary directly, set `DBX_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/dbx` to use `/var/lib/dbx/.dbx/secret.key` with the same lifecycle and backup rules. When upgrading from a release that stored credentials in plain text, Desktop and Web display a **Data Security Upgrade** wizard before opening the main application. Choose **Start upgrade** to create a restricted backup, migrate legacy database/JSON credentials, and verify that encrypted values can be read. Failures retain the original data and backup; fix the issue shown in the wizard and choose **Retry**. The backup path is shown after success. Once you have verified your connections, **Delete migration backups** asks for confirmation and removes the migration backup directory and the legacy JSON `.bak` files created by that migration. Unrelated backup files are kept. Users with no legacy data proceed directly after the initial check. Local CLI and standalone MCP can reuse the existing platform credential store on the same device, or read an explicitly configured `DBX_SECRET_KEY_FILE`/`DBX_SECRET_KEY`. They do not create keys during the startup check or automatically migrate legacy data. A `DATA_MIGRATION_REQUIRED` error means that you must first open the same data directory in Desktop or Web and complete its upgrade wizard. For headless hosts without a platform credential store, configure the persistent key. Cross-device exports use a separate sync passphrase and never contain the local storage key. For installed builds, or when copying only `dbx.db`, platform keys do not move with the database; use encrypted export/import instead. A Windows portable build must move the complete `data` directory containing both `dbx.db` and `.dbx/secret.key`. For the complete design, migration state machine, implementation map, troubleshooting, and test plan, see [DBX Data Security Upgrade and Migration](docs/data-security-migration.md). To publish DBX under a reverse-proxy context path such as `/dbx`, set the runtime base path and proxy the same prefix to the container: ```yaml environment: - DBX_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=/dbx ``` When building the frontend yourself with an absolute asset base, set `VITE_DBX_BASE_PATH=/dbx/` before `pnpm build`. ## Getting Started ### Prerequisites - [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) >= 18 - [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/) - [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install) >= 1.88 #### System Dependencies **macOS:** No additional dependencies required. **Linux (Ubuntu/Debian):** ```bash sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev libappindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf libssl-dev ``` **NIXOS/NIX :** See README-NIX.md **Windows:** No additional dependencies required. ### Development ```bash make ``` `make` installs root dependencies when needed and starts the local Tauri desktop development environment. Development builds can run alongside an installed DBX instance and share its local data, including connections and history. Avoid changing the same connection or global setting in both windows at once. > [!TIP] > DuckDB compilation takes a while. If you're not working on DuckDB features, > skip it to speed up local builds: > > ```bash > # Fast checks (skip DuckDB) > make cargo-check-fast > make cargo-test-fast > > # Tauri dev without DuckDB > make dev-fast > ``` > > The `--no-default-features` flag only affects local development. > Release builds (`pnpm tauri build`) always include DuckDB. Web version: ```bash make dev-web # frontend make dev-backend # backend ``` Documentation site: ```bash make docs ``` The official DBX documentation site lives in `docs/`. If you want to improve the website content or documentation pages, edit the files under `docs/` and run `make docs` to preview the site locally. Plugin authors should start with [Develop and Submit DBX Plugins](https://dbxio.com/en/docs/plugin-development). Plugin source normally stays in its own repository; Marketplace listing pull requests go to [`t8y2/dbx-store`](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx-store), while plugin host, SDK, and CLI changes go to this repository. For clean, reproducible local database instances, use the versioned Docker Compose recipes under [`deploy/database/`](deploy/database/README.md): ```bash make db-list make db-verify DB=mysql@8.4 ``` JDBC agent driver development projects live in `agents/`: ```bash cd agents ./gradlew test ``` Build artifacts from `agents/drivers//build/libs/` are picked up by local driver install flows when available. ### Build ```bash make package ``` The installer will be in `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/`. `pnpm build` explicitly removes the previous root `dist/` directory before running Vite, so desktop packaging starts with fresh frontend output. ## Tech Stack | Layer | Technology | | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Framework | [Tauri 2](https://tauri.app/) | | Frontend | [Vue 3](https://vuejs.org/) + TypeScript | | UI | [shadcn-vue](https://www.shadcn-vue.com/) + Tailwind CSS | | Editor | [CodeMirror 6](https://codemirror.net/) | | Backend | Rust + [sqlx](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx) / [tiberius](https://github.com/prisma/tiberius) / [redis-rs](https://github.com/redis-rs/redis-rs) / [mongodb](https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-rust-driver) | ## Documentation - [Official docs](https://dbxio.com/en/docs/what-is-dbx) — feature guides and tutorials - [Plugin development](https://dbxio.com/en/docs/plugin-development) — create plugins and submit Marketplace listings to the correct repository - [Database Test Lab](https://dbxio.com/en/docs/database-lab) — local database recipes for development and verification - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) — how to pick up issues and open PRs - [Web API reference](docs/content/docs/web-api.mdx) — HTTP API for Docker/Web deployments - [Examples](examples/) — CLI, MCP, Docker, and API samples ## Support DBX DBX is free and open source, but ongoing maintenance, database compatibility testing, infrastructure, and release work require sustained time and resources. - [Support DBX](https://my.feishu.cn/wiki/WMTkwdATDiiu4rk14JMcoyhTnoh) — voluntary donations via WeChat or Alipay - [Sponsors & Partners](https://my.feishu.cn/wiki/CgOWwwTzzify79k9Oq8cXpUNn6e) — sponsorship, infrastructure, tools, and community collaboration ## Contributors ## Community [![LINUX DO](https://img.shields.io/badge/LINUX%20DO-Community-blue)](https://linux.do) [![1Panel](https://img.shields.io/badge/1Panel-Partner-005EEB?logo=1panel&logoColor=white)](https://1panel.cn) ## Star History ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE)

# 无限五代 IG5 **DeepSeek Harness 最强开源逆向工程工作台** *静态分析 · 原生调试 · 单函数仿真 · 流量采集 · 解密恢复 · 协议还原 · 智能体协作*

**⭐ 4,100+ Stars · 🍴 530+ Forks · 📦 43 工具 · 🛠 8 技能 · 🚀 90 天 3 个正式版 · 📅 数据截至 2026-11-10** 🚀 快速安装 · ⚡ 30 秒看懂 · 🏆 方案对比 · ❓ FAQ · 📚 文档 · 💬 社区 · 🤖 llms.txt
--- **无限五代（Infinite Gen 5 / IG5，仓库 `dsh-infinite-gen-5`）** 是 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）生态中 **Star 数最高、功能最完整的开源逆向工程插件与可视化工作台**：**43 个分析工具、8 个工作流技能**，把 **Ghidra**（静态）+ **x64dbg**（原生调试）+ **Unicorn**（仿真）三引擎与流量采集、解密恢复、协议还原、多智能体协作全部接入同一套工作流。Windows x64 **自包含安装包开箱即用，不需要商业 IDA**。项目 2026-08-15 创建，**90 天内收获 4,100+ Stars、530+ Forks**，配套 85+ 篇技术文档（数据截至 2026-11-10）。 > **English TL;DR** — Infinite Gen 5 (IG5) is the most-starred open-source reverse-engineering plugin and visual workbench for **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**: **43 tools, 8 workflow skills**, and three engines — **Ghidra** (static), **x64dbg** (native debugging), **Unicorn** (emulation) — plus HTTP/HTTPS capture, crypto extraction and multi-agent investigation, all behind one DSH plugin. Ships as a self-contained Windows x64 installer; **no commercial IDA required**. 4,100+ stars within 90 days of launch. License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial). > 仅限自有或合法授权目标的逆向工程、安全审计与教学研究。项目独立维护，与 DeepSeek 官方无隶属或官方背书关系。技术社区论坛：[OpenOrigin](https://openorigin.link/) --- ## ⚡ 30 秒看懂 IG5 | | | | | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | **⭐ 4,100+**

核心速览 | 项目 | 数据（截至 2026-11-10） | | :--- | :--- | | 定位 | DeepSeek Harness（DSH）生态最强开源逆向工程插件与可视化工作台 | | 工具面 | **43 个工具** = Core 8（默认）+ 28 静态入口 + 13 审批入口 + 2 生命周期 | | 工作流技能 | **8 个原生技能**（triage / deep-dive / patch-and-sign / diff / debug-live / crypto / protocol / reverse-agent） | | 斜杠命令 | **10 条** `/ig5 *` 宿主命令，无需模型先生成工具调用 | | 分析引擎 | **Ghidra**（静态）+ **x64dbg**（原生调试）+ **Unicorn**（单函数仿真） | | 网络能力 | 内置 HTTP/HTTPS 采集、显式 TLS 解密、PCAP/PCAPNG 解析、请求重放 | | 安装方式 | Windows x64 **自包含安装包**（内置 Ghidra/JDK/Python、x64dbg/bridge），解压 + 一条命令 | | 宿主兼容 | `@deepseek-ai/dsh >=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`（已验证 `0.2.1-alpha.1`） | | 许可 | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0（免费开源，非商业使用） |
## 🏆 为什么选 IG5（与其他方案对比） | 能力维度 | **IG5** | IDA Pro | 裸 Ghidra | 通用 MCP 插件 | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | DSH 智能体工作流原生集成 | ✅ | ❌ | ⚠️ 需自建脚本 | ⚠️ 浅层封装 | | 静态 + 调试 + 仿真三引擎一体 | ✅ | ⚠️ 需付费插件 | ⚠️ | ❌ | | 内置 HTTP/HTTPS 采集与 TLS 解密 | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | 子代理协作 · 持久调查 · 证据 dossier | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | 自包含安装（免商业授权） | ✅ 一次解压 | ❌ 需购买授权 | ⚠️ 手动配环境 | ⚠️ | | AI 审批安全模型 + 审计回溯 | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | 成本 | **免费** | 数千美元/席位 | 免费 | 免费 | **五个决定性差异：** 1. **生态内唯一全链路** — 静态分析、原生调试、单函数仿真、流量采集、解密恢复、协议还原、去混淆研究与子代理协作，一个插件全覆盖，不需要在多个工具之间搬运上下文。 2. **AI 原生证据链** — 单函数 dossier（伪代码 + CFG + 调用关系 + 栈帧，同一数据库修订）、持久调查任务、stale 证据标记、共享调用预算——把"模型推测"与"已验证结论"分开，这是给 AI 用的逆向工作台与 GUI 套壳的本质区别。 3. **零配置自包含** — 完整安装包内置 Ghidra/JDK/Python 与 x64dbg/bridge 及上游源码、许可与哈希清单，一次解压 + 一条 PowerShell 命令完成安装，全程不需要商业 IDA。 4. **审批安全模型** — 13 个修改/执行入口全部经过宿主审批（`allowed-once`），配合 Undo、审计流水与 SHA-256 哈希清单，适合团队与教学环境的可控授权分析。 5. **增长最快的 DSH 逆向插件** — 上线 90 天 4,100+ Stars、530+ Forks，Star 增速居 DSH 插件生态首位；85 篇文档与 Release 节奏持续更新。 ## ✨ 七大能力域 | 方向 | 主要能力 | 使用边界 | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 🔍 静态分析 | 函数、字符串、交叉引用、反编译、CFG、类型、结构体、虚表与跳转表检视 | 支持情况依赖具体后端；部分分析与未决结果保留标记 | | 🖼 可视化工作台 | SVG CFG 平移/缩放、双击查看汇编、局部变量焦点高亮、结构体草稿与审计时间线 | 焦点行过滤不等于完整污点分析；编辑草稿仍需发送并审批 | | 🐞 调试与仿真 | x64dbg 原生调试、断点、寄存器/内存、受限轨迹；Unicorn 单函数仿真 | 执行需要授权和审批；仿真不提供完整 OS、import 或 TLS 环境 | | 🌐 HTTP/HTTPS 采集 | 本机代理、显式 TLS 解密、流量历史、证据导出、请求重放与下发载荷提取 | 仅批准 origin；不自动修改系统代理或证书信任，不等同完整 Burp 功能 | | 🔐 解密与协议 | 编码/压缩检查、XOR/AES、有界候选检索、PCAP/PCAPNG 解析、分帧与观察状态模型 | 不保证未知密钥恢复或隐藏服务器语义；缺口、冲突与外推假设保留 | | 🧩 IR 与去混淆研究 | 真实 p-code/SSA、单函数只读去混淆覆盖层、路径投影、状态组合与离线轨迹恢复 | 局部模型或数学证明不等于通用去壳、完整 VM 或业务恢复 | | 🤝 调查与子代理协作 | 单函数 dossier、持久调查任务、受控 handoff、证据回交与根会话共享调用预算 | DSH 负责派工；插件核验身份/证据/生命周期，不认证模型理解或结论正确性 | **典型适用场景**（按优先级）： 1. 新样本快速分诊 — 架构识别、字符串/熵扫描、关键函数定位（`/ig5-triage`） 2. 单函数深挖与类型恢复 — 伪代码、CFG、调用方/被调方、栈帧一次拿全（`ig5_decompile style=dossier`） 3. 授权目标的动态验证 — 断点、寄存器、内存、API 轨迹（`/ig5-debug-live`） 4. 通信协议与配置提取 — 抓包分帧、XOR/AES 候选、状态模型验证（`/ig5-protocol`、`/ig5-crypto`） 5. 版本差异与补丁分析 — `ig5_bindiff` 候选变更块 + 调用关系/常量/虚表核验（`/ig5-diff`） 6. 长周期自主调查 — 持久任务、证据保存、失败分流、子代理 handoff（`/ig5-reverse-agent`） 能力边界与逐项验收记录见 [能力矩阵](docs/CAPABILITIES.md) 与 [已知限制](docs/LIMITATIONS.md)。 --- ## 🚀 快速安装 ### Windows x64（推荐，约 3 分钟） 需要已安装的 DeepSeek Harness profile。完整包内置 Ghidra/JDK/Python、x64dbg/Python/bridge 和上游源码、许可及哈希清单；**不需要商业 IDA 安装**，DSH 本身不随包提供。 1. 从 [v1.3.0 Release](https://github.com/Minglink/dsh-infinite-gen-5/releases/tag/v1.3.0) 下载 `IG5-1.3.0-Windows-x64-portable-full.zip` 和同名 `.sha256`，核对 SHA-256：`04273147dde23976a625c582773c33ca1df7b851da0bd5a6e52e2a7c6530b815` 2. 完整解压，保留 `plugin/`、`manifest.json` 及所有运行资产；不要只复制安装脚本 3. 在解压根目录打开 PowerShell，执行： ```powershell & .\plugin\install.ps1 ``` 4. 完全退出并重启 DSH，执行 `/ig5 engines` 和 `ig5_doctor` 检查实际可用性 5. 本地 1.3.0 安装后用 `ig5_profile` 核对 `version=1.3.0`、`implementationRevision=20261026-release-1.3.0`，确认新实现已加载 > [!NOTE] > **Source code ZIP / tar.gz 与 git clone 是维护源码，不是完整离线安装包。** 普通安装请下载上述命名的 Windows 完整 ZIP。仅切换插件开关可能复用旧模块，更新后应冷启动 DSH。
📦 源码安装、离线资产复用与修复 在最新源码根目录执行： ```powershell & .\install.ps1 ``` 源码安装器首次联网获取固定供体，仅补齐 `runtimes/` 和 `third_party/sources/`，不覆盖当前插件代码。`scripts/distribution.json` 仍固定到 [1.0.0 资产基线](https://github.com/Minglink/dsh-infinite-gen-5/releases/tag/v1.0.0-dsh021-20261010)，这只是原生依赖供体，不表示当前源码回退到 1.0.0。 已有原始固定 ZIP 时可离线复用，文件必须放在源码目录之外： ```powershell & .\install.ps1 -DistributionArchive 'D:\IG5-1.0.0-Windows-x64-dsh021-full-20261010.zip' -Offline ``` 固定供体 ZIP 的 SHA-256：`a2459ddca1f19e5eec2d7918c504f133889809800a0b277e1e379d3ce1459b54`。这是 **1.0.0 供体**的校验值，不是 1.3.0 完整 ZIP 的校验值。 也可使用已核验、包含 `manifest.json` 和 `plugin/` 的完整解压根目录： ```powershell & .\install.ps1 -DistributionRoot 'C:\已解压的完整发行包根目录' -Offline ``` `-DistributionArchive` 与 `-DistributionRoot` 不能同时使用。只传 `-Offline` 但缺少完整资产时，安装器会拒绝并给出指引。 包含 `-RepairAssets` 参数的新安装器完整包，在核心代码仍与外层清单一致时，可显式修复运行资产： ```powershell & .\plugin\install.ps1 -RepairAssets -DistributionArchive 'D:\IG5-1.0.0-Windows-x64-dsh021-full-20261010.zip' -Offline ``` 不要把新安装脚本单独拷入旧的哈希封存包。SHA 不符时保留相对路径、Expected/Actual SHA-256 和大小，先核对原始 ZIP；不能直接归咎某个解压工具。维护者重建说明见 [BUILD](docs/BUILD.md)。
### 其他平台与宿主兼容 - **macOS Apple Silicon** — 实验性 `darwin-arm64` Ghidra 静态车道，需要独立准备运行包；Windows ZIP 和 `install.ps1` 不适用。不支持 x64dbg/Windows 原生调试，也不包含可用的 macOS Unicorn 运行时。见 [macOS 指南](docs/MACOS_RUNTIME.md) - **Android / iOS** — 未完成真机验收或原生运行包。支持 ARM64 目标分析，不等于支持手机宿主 - **DSH** — 声明范围为 `@deepseek-ai/dsh >=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`，宿主按 `includePrerelease: true` 判断。已记录验证的宿主为 `0.2.1-alpha.1`，不代表范围内所有版本都实测通过。见 [兼容记录](docs/DSH_COMPATIBILITY.md) ## 🧭 开始一次调查（5 步） 1. 用 `/ig5 engines` 确认后端，再用 `/ig5 open --engine ghidra <样本路径>` 打开目标；打开不启动样本 2. 从函数、字符串和交叉引用定位问题，用 `ig5_decompile style=dossier` 获取同一修订下的伪代码、CFG、调用关系和栈帧证据 3. 需要持续调查时，通过 `ig5_workspace` 保存目标、进度与假设；旧 attachment 或修订的证据会标为 stale。详见 [调查工作流](docs/INVESTIGATION_WORKFLOW.md) 4. 需要高级工具时切换 Full 43；补丁、调试、仿真、重放等操作仍须单独审批 5. 子代理任务由 DSH 原生派工。IG5 支持 `handoff → claim → evidence → submit → 子代理完成 → review`，正式复核必须绑定同一交接和实际生命周期。见 [子代理工作流](docs/SUBAGENT_WORKFLOW.md) 父、子及后代共享的 IG5 调用预算须显式启用，例如 `ig5_profile collaboration={action:"start",max_calls:20}`；状态查询用 `collaboration={action:"status"}`。额度不从提示词自动推断，不计 token 或非 IG5 工具；重复 start 或重载不能放大额度。证据提交和正式复核仍不等于语义结论认证。 ## ⌨️ 常用指令与工具 ### 斜杠命令 ```text /ig5 status /ig5 engines /ig5 open --engine ghidra <样本路径> /ig5 toolset full /ig5 toolset core /ig5 deobfuscate --engine ghidra <十六进制函数地址> <样本路径> /ig5 state <轨迹JSON完整路径> /ig5 state-validate <推断报告UUID> <新轨迹JSON完整路径> /ig5 export --engine ghidra <样本路径> ``` 斜杠命令直接走宿主命令入口，无需模型先生成工具调用。`state-validate` 默认验证保存的前缀树；验证合并假设需用 `ig5_protocol` 显式指定模型。 ### Core 8 / Full 43 默认 **Core 8**：`ig5_doctor`、`ig5_open`、`ig5_status`、`ig5_funcs`、`ig5_strings`、`ig5_decompile`、`ig5_close`、`ig5_profile` **Full 43** = **28 非审批静态入口 + 13 审批入口 + 2 生命周期/配置**。"静态"指不执行目标、不开引擎、不发网络，但不等于不写文件：`ig5_workspace` 会更新本会话任务存储并写不可变报告，`ig5_recovery` 会写不可变报告，`ig5_package unpack` 会写解包文件。支持 scoped API 的 DSH 只向当前 agent 展开 Full；旧宿主明确返回 `toolsetScope=plugin-instance`。切换不持久化，也不授予执行或写入权限。
📄 展开完整工具清单（43） **静态、无目标执行（28）** `ig5_doctor` · `ig5_open` · `ig5_status` · `ig5_funcs` · `ig5_strings` · `ig5_decompile` · `ig5_xrefs` · `ig5_calls` · `ig5_bytes` · `ig5_search` · `ig5_listing` · `ig5_scan` · `ig5_export_diff` · `ig5_cfg` · `ig5_slice` · `ig5_fingerprint` · `ig5_stack` · `ig5_switches` · `ig5_vtables` · `ig5_microcode` · `ig5_bindiff` · `ig5_ir` · `ig5_crypto` · `ig5_protocol` · `ig5_capture` · `ig5_package` · `ig5_workspace` · `ig5_recovery` > 其中 `ig5_open` 管理会话与驱动库，`ig5_workspace`/`ig5_recovery`/`ig5_package unpack` 会写任务存储或文件；它们都不执行样本、不开调试会话、不发网络请求。 **审批入口（13）** `ig5_rename` · `ig5_patch_bytes` · `ig5_comment` · `ig5_analyze` · `ig5_set_type` · `ig5_undo` · `ig5_run_idapython` · `ig5_dbg` · `ig5_struct` · `ig5_switch_repair` · `ig5_emulate` · `ig5_sync` · `ig5_capture_control` > 审批入口只在宿主返回 `allowed-once` 后继续后续策略；拒绝、服务不可用、未知结果或异常均不执行，取消保持取消。Undo 范围以具体后端为准，不能假设所有修改都可回滚。 **生命周期/配置（2）** `ig5_close` · `ig5_profile`
### 八个原生工作流技能 | 技能 | 适用场景 | | :--- | :--- | | `/ig5-triage` | 新样本首探：架构、字符串、熵与关键假设 | | `/ig5-deep-dive` | 单函数深挖：分支、CFG、变量与类型 | | `/ig5-patch-and-sign` | 补丁实验、原字节校验、审批与 SHA-256 签收（不是代码签名证书签发） | | `/ig5-diff` | 版本差异与候选变更块定位 | | `/ig5-debug-live` | 已授权目标的断点与动态验证 | | `/ig5-crypto` | 解密与配置提取，核对参数和产物来源 | | `/ig5-protocol` | 捕获、分帧、字段证据与状态模型验证 | | `/ig5-reverse-agent` | 持续调查、证据保存、失败分流与逐项验收 | 持续运行依赖 DSH 原生 Goal 驱动，技能提供方法与判断约束；注册成功或一条最终回复不代表完整自主能力。见 [自主逆向](docs/AGENT_AUTONOMY.md)。 --- ## ❓ FAQ（高频问题直答） **IG5 是什么？** 无限五代（Infinite Gen 5 / IG5，仓库 `dsh-infinite-gen-5`）是面向 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）的开源逆向工程插件与可视化工作台，提供 43 个工具、8 个工作流技能，把 Ghidra 静态分析、x64dbg 原生调试、Unicorn 仿真、HTTP/HTTPS 流量采集与解密、多智能体调查协作整合进同一套 DSH 工作流。 **IG5 与 IDA Pro / Binary Ninja 是什么关系？** 互补而非替代。IG5 使用 Ghidra 作为静态后端并内置完整运行时，**安装 IG5 不需要购买任何商业反编译器授权**；已有 IDA 的用户也可以通过 `ig5_run_idapython`（审批入口）在授权环境中复用现有脚本。 **IG5 免费吗？采用什么许可证？** 免费开源，采用 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0（署名-非商业性使用-相同方式共享）。可自由用于个人研究、安全审计、CTF 与教学；商业售卖、付费倒卖与二开商用被明确禁止，详见文末许可声明。 **怎么安装 IG5？** Windows x64 用户从 [v1.3.0 Release](https://github.com/Minglink/dsh-infinite-gen-5/releases/tag/v1.3.0) 下载自包含安装包，解压后在根目录执行 `& .\plugin\install.ps1`，重启 DSH 后用 `/ig5 engines` 验证。完整步骤见[快速安装](#local-install)。 **IG5 支持哪些平台？** Windows x64 完整支持（安装包内置全部运行时）；macOS Apple Silicon 提供实验性 Ghidra 静态车道；目标侧支持 x86/x64/ARM64 等架构的静态分析。详见 [macOS 指南](docs/MACOS_RUNTIME.md) 与 [DSH 兼容记录](docs/DSH_COMPATIBILITY.md)。 **IG5 能做什么、不能做什么？** 能做：静态分析、可视化 CFG 工作台、原生调试、单函数仿真、流量采集与 TLS 解密、XOR/AES 解密候选、协议分帧与状态建模、CFF/VM 去混淆研究、子代理协作调查。边界：所有执行/修改类操作需宿主审批；不承诺"任意保护一键脱壳"；局部模型不外推为通用恢复。完整口径见 [能力矩阵](docs/CAPABILITIES.md) 与 [已知限制](docs/LIMITATIONS.md)。 **IG5 和 DeepSeek 官方是什么关系？** 完全独立的第三方开源项目，与 DeepSeek 官方或其关联主体无隶属、无商业合作、无官方背书。IG5 通过 DSH 插件机制扩展宿主能力，DSH 本身不随 IG5 分发。 **为什么 IG5 要做 13 个审批门？** 安全模型设计。所有修改字节、执行样本、仿真、重放、采集控制入口都必须经宿主显式审批（`allowed-once`），配合 Undo、审计流水与 SHA-256 哈希清单，让 AI 驱动的逆向操作在授权范围内可审计、可控、可回溯——这是 IG5 与"裸工具包"类插件的核心差异。 **IG5 的版本节奏如何？** 2026-08-15 创建以来已发布 v1.0.0、v1.1.0、v1.3.0 三个正式版本（90 天内），当前最新版 v1.3.0（2026-10-27）将工具面扩展至 Full 43 并新增 APK/固件静态前端、API trace 与 CFF 状态分析。历史版本见 [Releases](https://github.com/Minglink/dsh-infinite-gen-5/releases)。 **如何在论文/报告中引用 IG5？** 推荐引用格式：`Minglink, "Infinite Gen 5 (IG5): An Open-Source Reverse-Engineering Workbench Plugin for DeepSeek Harness", GitHub repository dsh-infinite-gen-5, 2026. https://github.com/Minglink/dsh-infinite-gen-5`（引用时请注明所用版本号与访问日期）。 --- ## repositories.readme:
Sketch Material 3 Expressive screens in the browser, link them, tap through them, and copy a prompt for your AI coding tool.


Sketch the screens, tap through the flow, copy the prompt, and let your AI coding tool build the app. (mp4)

M3E Canvas is a free, open-source sketchpad for app screens made of real Material 3 Expressive parts. It runs entirely in your browser: no account, no server, nothing to install. What you sketch becomes a precise prompt that any AI coding tool that takes one, such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Cursor, can turn into a working app.

## How it works 1. **Sketch** — Drag parts onto phone or desktop screens. They snap together and line up on a 4dp grid. 2. **Tap through** — Link parts to screens and press Preview to try the flow, transitions included. 3. **Copy the prompt** — The whole design becomes a short brief in your language. Paste it into your AI coding tool. ## What's inside **Real M3 Expressive parts** — Buttons, FABs, bars, tabs, cards, lists, sheets, pickers, carousels, loading indicators and more, each with its own panel for text, style, size and what a tap does. **Screens and flow** — Phone and desktop screens, screens that scroll, taps and swipes that open other screens with the transition you pick, and arrows that show the whole flow. **Theme in one place** — Color, shape, type and motion: seven palettes or your own seed color, light and dark, three contrast levels, corner styles, fonts and the expressive spring motion. **Optional AI help** — Bring your own key to draft a design or write notes for you, or copy an instruction for a coding agent that replies with a share link. Keys never leave your browser.
Everything it can do - **Parts** – buttons, icon buttons, FABs and extended FABs, FAB menus, split buttons, chips, top app bars, navigation bars and rails, floating toolbars, tabs, search bars, cards, list items, boxes, bottom sheets, dialogs, snackbars, text fields, dropdowns, switches, checkboxes, radio buttons, sliders, date and time pickers, text, images, carousels, camera and map placeholders, dividers, the shape-morphing loading indicator and wavy progress indicators. Every part has a panel for its text, style, size and alignment, and a trigger tab for what a tap does. - **Magnetic connections** – bring buttons, chips or list items close and they fuse into a connected group; the corners soften where they meet. - **Phone and desktop screens** – add as many screens as you like. Switch any screen between a 412×892 phone and a 1280×800 desktop from its label: bars stretch, a navigation bar becomes a rail and back again, and the parts are laid out again. Same-named screens are written into the prompt as one screen at two widths. - **Screens that scroll** – make a screen longer than its device and its body scrolls under the bars in the preview. Drag the grip on the bottom bezel, or pick 1x to 3x in the screen panel. - **Tap and swipe to navigate** – give any tappable part, app bar icon or navigation destination a target screen (or "back") and a transition: slide from any side, fade, expand or none. Screens can also open others on a swipe. The preview plays it all, and back runs in reverse. - **Layers and groups** – a layers panel per screen to change the stacking order; group parts to keep their overlap and move them as one, then copy and paste whole selections across screens. - **Theme** – seven palettes or one seed color that becomes a full Material 3 scheme you can fine-tune, light and dark, three contrast levels and dynamic color. Square, rounded or full corners for every part at once. Roboto, Roboto Flex, Roboto Serif or the system font. The standard or the expressive spring motion, which also drives the preview. - **Prompt** – the whole design or a single screen as a concise brief in Japanese, English, Chinese or Korean, with your notes on what each part does. Rows, overlaps and aligned grids of cards are spelled out, so the generated layout keeps them. Choose Android or the web as the target, edit the text before copying, or save a screen as a PNG. - **Tidy** – one button snaps bars to the edges and the FAB to the corner, joins neighbouring items, and stacks the rest on 16dp margins. Press it again to undo. - **AI helper (optional)** – bring your own key for OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or DeepSeek to draft a design from a sentence or write a part's behaviour note and a screen's description. Every rewrite can be undone. The request goes straight from your browser to the provider. - **Share links** – copy a link that opens your design on anyone's canvas, or an instruction for Claude Code, Codex or another agent: it reads [agent.md](public/agent.md), sketches what you described, and replies with such a link. - **Everything else** – alignment guides and a 4dp grid, undo and redo, keyboard shortcuts, a keyboard-usable parts panel, favorites, install as an app, and autosave in your browser. - **On a phone** – one fixed screen and a buttons-only editor with bottom sheets. The full editor is for desktop browsers.
## Keyboard | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | `V` / `H` | Select / hand tool (hold `Space` to pan) | | Wheel, `Ctrl` + wheel | Pan, zoom | | `+` `-` `0` | Zoom in, zoom out, fit | | `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` | Undo / redo | | `Ctrl+C` / `Ctrl+V` | Copy / paste parts, also across screens | | `Ctrl+D` | Duplicate | | `Ctrl+G` / `Ctrl+Shift+G` | Group / ungroup | | `Shift` + click | Add to the selection | | Arrows (`Shift` = 8dp) | Nudge | | `Ctrl` + drag | Move without snapping (no guides, no 4dp grid) | | `Delete` | Delete part or screen | | `P` | Preview | ## Run it locally ```bash npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:3000 npm run build # static export to ./out ``` The app is a static Next.js export. To host it under a sub-path (for example a GitHub Pages project site), set `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=/your-repo` at build time. `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` does this and publishes `out/` to GitHub Pages on every push to `main`. ## Contributing Bug reports, part requests and pull requests are welcome. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) explains the setup, the conventions (English comments, four languages for every string) and where each kind of change lives. Questions go to [Discussions](https://github.com/lnkiai/m3e-canvas/discussions). ## Support M3E Canvas is free and MIT-licensed, and stays that way. If it saves you time, you can [sponsor the work on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/lnkiai); it pays for the hours that go into new parts, the prompt, and reviewing contributions. No feature is behind sponsorship.

Thanks to the sponsors who keep this going:

## Thanks Thanks to everyone who has contributed code, ideas and reviews:

## Credits - Loading indicator shapes and animation model: [material-components-android](https://github.com/material-components/material-components-android) (Apache-2.0) via [Aler1x/m3-loading-indicator](https://github.com/Aler1x/m3-loading-indicator). See `NOTICE`. - Icons: [Material Symbols](https://fonts.google.com/icons) (Apache-2.0). Fonts are loaded from Google Fonts. ## See also - [matraic/m3e](https://github.com/matraic/m3e) – Material 3 Expressive as Lit web components (MIT), with React bindings and an icon package. A good home for the screens you sketch here. - [Beer CSS](https://www.beercss.com/) – Material Design 3 as a plain CSS framework (MIT). Another way to build the web version of a screen you sketch here. ## Contact For anything that does not fit an issue, such as collaboration or press, get in touch:
